q: Why can Dijkstra finalise the node it pops from the heap?
options: All other routes are at least as long, and non-negative edges can't make them shorter
why: Any other path already costs ≥ this distance before adding more non-negative edges.

q: What goes wrong with negative edge weights?
options: A settled node could later be reached more cheaply

q: Dijkstra with a binary heap costs…
why: Each edge may push to the heap; each push/pop is O(log V).

q: All edges have the same cost. What's simplest?
why: BFS already finds fewest-edge paths in O(V + E).

q: Cheapest Flights with at most k stops: why relax from a COPY of last round's distances?
options: So one round extends paths by at most one flight
why: Updating in place could chain several flights in a single round and break the stop limit.

q: Network Delay: distances from the source are [0, 3, 5, 2]. Answer?
why: The signal reaches everyone when the farthest node gets it: the maximum distance.
